findings.title: Team admin/owner check uses AND instead of OR
findings.body: In addGuests.handler.ts the authorization check computes isTeamAdminOrOwner as (await isTeamAdmin(...)) && (await isTeamOwner(...)). A user is rarely both admin AND owner, so legitimate team admins or owners who are not the organizer/attendee will be rejected with FORBIDDEN, while the intent was to allow either role. It should be ||. Consequence: team management cannot add guests unless they are also the booking owner.

findings.title: Blacklist and duplicate checks are case-sensitive and bypassable
findings.body: In addGuests.handler.ts blacklisted emails are lowercased when loaded from BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS, but the incoming guest value is compared without lowercasing: !blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest). Similarly existing attendees are compared with guest === attendee.email. An attacker can bypass the blacklist and create duplicate attendee rows by changing case (e.g. Foo@bar.com vs foo@bar.com). The server also does not deduplicate duplicates within the request itself. Consequence: blacklist ineffective and duplicate Attendee records.

findings.title: Unbounded guests array allows email/DB spam
findings.body: In addGuests.schema.ts the input is z.array(z.string().email()) with no min/max length, uniqueness, or normalization. A single authorized caller (including any existing attendee) can submit hundreds/thousands of emails in one request. The handler then creates that many Attendee rows, updates the calendar, and fans out to sendAddGuestsEmails for every attendee. Consequence: DB bloat, calendar API abuse, and mass unsolicited email (spam/DoS) from the victim organizer's booking.

findings.title: Sends emails using unfiltered guests list instead of uniqueGuests
findings.body: In addGuests.handler.ts the handler filters input into uniqueGuests (removing existing attendees and blacklisted addresses) for the DB insert, but then calls sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests) with the original unfiltered array. In email-manager.ts newGuests.includes(attendee.email) is used to decide between AttendeeScheduledEmail for new guests vs AttendeeAddGuestsEmail for old attendees. Consequence: a re-submitted existing attendee in a mixed request is misclassified as new and gets the wrong invitation email, and blacklisted addresses influence routing.

findings.title: No validation of booking status or time before adding guests
findings.body: In addGuests.handler.ts after loading the booking the handler only checks existence and permission, then immediately inserts new Attendee rows, updates the external calendar via EventManager, and sends emails. It never rejects cancelled, rejected, or already-ended bookings. The UI also exposes the action for past confirmed bookings. Consequence: guests can be added to cancelled/past events, corrupting calendar state and sending confusing add-guest emails for events that will never happen.

findings.title: Calendar update uses requestor credentials instead of organizer credentials
findings.body: In addGuests.handler.ts the booking query eagerly loads booking.user.credentials and destinationCalendar, but they are never used. Instead credentials are loaded with getUsersCredentials(ctx.user) where ctx.user is the caller, who may be any attendee, and EventManager is constructed from the caller. The calendar event is owned by the organizer, not the attendee. Consequence: when an attendee adds guests the calendar update runs with the wrong account's tokens and will fail or update the wrong calendar, leaving external calendars out of sync with the DB.
